extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, assessment coordinators, and administrators responsible for undergraduate mathematics programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplar assessment practices for evaluating undergraduate mathematics majors (capstone courses, seminars, comprehensive exams, focus groups, portfolios, and program-level outcomes). Includes specific assignment-level criteria and department-level assessment cycle requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar as curriculum-integrated assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the seminar a required part of the department's educational program (graded for academic credit) so assessment is embedded in learning rather than an added testing requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach the seminar as a learning tool to minimize participation problems; tie it to standard content where possible so students' schedules are not unduly disrupted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit requirements, deadlines, and grading criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements, deadlines, dates, and grading criteria must be explicit and clear from the beginning to prevent students (especially weaker ones) from falling behind and to avoid misunderstandings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make grading criteria as explicit as possible and communicate formats and deadlines to all faculty and students early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full faculty involvement and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: All faculty must support the program, keep track of deadlines and paper formats, be willing to serve on committees, and adjust schedules when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seminar director should coordinate and resolve interpretive differences, but program cannot function without broad faculty buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of time costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for increased use of student time (two-semester seminar, comprehensive project) and faculty time (one-on-one mentoring, written critiques, long advising commitments) when designing the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that seminar directors and project advisors spend more time than typical course preparation; plan workloads and credit accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — independent reading competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase student competence in the independent reading of mathematical materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assigned readings, short talks on journal articles, and reading-based summaries to develop and assess this skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — review, structure, and apply mathematical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable students to review, structure, and apply mathematical knowledge acquired throughout their program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use capstone projects, content-based exam problems, and group problem-solving to evaluate this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — develop skills for presenting rigorous arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop students' abilities to present rigorous mathematical arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess via oral presentations, expository papers, and class discussions emphasizing logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — organize and deliver mathematical presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach and assess students' ability to organize and deliver a mathematical presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staged speaking assignments (5-minute practice talks followed by a 25-minute project presentation) with preset evaluation criteria and peer/instructor feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — pursue topics beyond prior coursework
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide opportunities for students to pursue mathematical topics not covered in previous courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow topic choice for the expository project and include exploratory readings and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — deepen previous topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable students to explore in greater depth several topics that have been studied earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use projects and readings that extend prior course material into advanced perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — develop group problem-solving skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate group problem-solving abilities through small-group problem sessions and rotating group membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both individual correctness on group tasks and team interaction (participation) points to measure collaboration and leadership development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — improve resource/technology skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve students' skills in utilizing resources: library, internet, professional networking, and career-related information retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scavenger-hunt style assignments graded on correctness to measure resource skills; encourage use of career services for resume work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — develop a global perspective on mathematics in society
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster a broad perspective on the role of mathematics in society (historical, ethical, philosophical, diverse contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess through class discussions of preassigned readings and open-ended reflective questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of short practice talks (peer feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: For short (5-minute) talks, classmates identify at least one positive and one negative attribute in writing; the instructor uses a known set of criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide immediate peer and instructor feedback; use the first talk as formative input for the second practice talk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of longer oral presentations (instructor and faculty panel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 25-minute project oral presentation is assessed by the instructor via written evaluations based on preset criteria and by a three-member faculty team using a pass/fail evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty panel evaluates the student's apparent level of understanding and the cohesion of the talk; instructor uses the same preset criteria students have been taught.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class discussion assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess class discussion performance based on (1) understanding the main idea of assigned readings and (2) conveying individual interpretations of the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these two criteria for grading participation in discussions on historical, ethical, philosophical, and diversity-related readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal assessment (holistic grading and self-assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students keep weekly journals (3–5 entries/week) reflecting thoughts on mathematics; journals are holistically graded three times and used by students for partial self-assessment on the final exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use holistic scoring rubrics and require journal-based reflection on attitudes and study habits for summative evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading-summary assignments (holistic, diagnostic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summaries of assigned articles are graded holistically and used primarily for diagnostic purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize comprehension and synthesis rather than fine-grained grammar grading in these diagnostic summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository paper evaluation (draft and final criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 20-page expository project paper is guided through stages; drafts are highly scrutinized (no grade) using preselected criteria such as knowledge of the subject, breadth of research, clarity of ideas, and overall flow; final paper is graded using the same criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide formative feedback on drafts using the rubric items; make explicit the criteria students will be judged on for the final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource/retrieval skills grading (correctness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments that probe library/internet/research skills (e.g., scavenger hunts) are graded on correctness of answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design concrete questions that require locating and synthesizing biographical/publication information or web-based resources; score for factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group problem-solving and participation grading
rubrics_metrics.description: For small-group mathematical problem sessions, award individual grades for correct solutions and class participation points for team interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate groups to develop leadership in each student; assess both individual mastery and collaborative behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final examination components (content questions and portfolio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final exam composed of (1) content-based problems measuring mathematical knowledge (including problems worked in small groups) and (2) a portfolio plus open-ended questions asking students to compare/contrast perspectives from readings and writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both computational/technical problems and reflective/open-ended items to capture breadth and depth of student learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio assessment (breadth and unification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Student portfolios focus on perceived mathematical growth over the term; assessment is based on the breadth of perceived learning and how the portfolio items are unified, using preselected criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask students to write a unifying essay connecting artifacts; allow inclusion of materials beyond the seminar; use a rubric emphasizing coherence and evidence of growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of assessment findings to redesign curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate assessment results into program changes (e.g., add oral assignments in other courses, require scientific writing before capstone, integrate more writing across curriculum, and improve advising about career-specific skill gaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identified weaknesses (writing, resource skills, technology, career preparation) to target curricular or advising interventions, and monitor effects in subsequent cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — read and interpret mathematical literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will read and interpret mathematical literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reading assignments and assess via summaries, talks, and comprehension tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — read and interpret graphical and numerical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will read and interpret graphical and numerical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess using data interpretation tasks and graphical representation exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — use mathematical symbols correctly and precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will use mathematical symbols correctly and precisely in expressing mathematical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate notation accuracy and precision in written work and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — represent quantitative information graphically
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will represent quantitative information by means of appropriate graphing techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tasks requiring selection and construction of appropriate graphs with commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — present well-structured and valid mathematical arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will present well-structured and valid mathematical arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proofs, essays, and oral presentations for logical coherence and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — employ critical thinking in comprehension and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will employ critical thinking skills in their comprehension and application of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use problem sets, essay prompts, and oral questioning to probe critical thinking and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — analyze and construct logical arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will analyze and construct logical arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure via proof-writing assignments and critique exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — discover patterns and formulate conjectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will discover mathematical patterns and formulate conjectures by exploration and experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exploratory lab/problem activities and evaluate the quality of conjectures and subsequent justification attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — express problems in mathematical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will express problems in mathematical terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess students' ability to mathematize real-world scenarios and model them appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — identify mathematics useful for practical problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will identify areas of mathematics that are most useful in solving practical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include application-focused assignments and reflective questions on applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — use technology appropriately in problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will use technology appropriately in solving problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess appropriate tool selection and interpretation of computational output (graphing calculators, computers, software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — appreciate the beauty and power of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will give examples of the beauty and power of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reflective writing, presentations, and readings to elicit and assess students' aesthetic and conceptual appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment cycle and methodology requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate on a multi-year assessment cycle (four-year recommended) during which outcomes are reviewed, data-collection methods chosen, and data collected and analyzed according to a timetable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over the cycle each program must collect at least one direct measure (tests, capstone courses, portfolios), one indirect measure (focus groups, exit interviews), and a survey of program alumni; plan to collect data one semester and analyze in the next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mixed measures (direct, indirect, alumni surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a variety of assessment techniques (in-house mathematics tests, alumni surveys, faculty surveys, focus groups) to obtain a broad picture and check consistency across measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangulate findings from multiple methods to identify consistent strengths/weaknesses; do not rely on a single data source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus groups — procedural conduct guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct graduating-senior focus groups after final grades are submitted, invite all seniors, provide a relaxed atmosphere, use faculty who did not teach those seniors, distribute questions in advance, have one faculty ask questions and another record, and encourage open, collegial discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule conveniently, remind participants, choose open-ended questions, wait patiently for responses, accept negative comments without defensiveness, and encourage students to respond to each other's remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus group question content (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask focused, open-ended questions such as 'What are your initial feelings about your experience as a mathematics major?', 'Do you have strong feelings about specific courses?', 'In what areas do you feel most prepared?', and 'If you could make one change in the department, what would it be and why?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these prompts to elicit concrete perceptions and suggestions; encourage elaboration and cross-commentary among participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caution — treat perceptions as perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that focus groups and alumni surveys capture perceptions which may include factual inaccuracies and may differ from faculty views; interpret them as subjective input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use perceptions to guide inquiry and reform but corroborate with objective measures before making factual conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using findings to implement specific curricular changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate focus-group and assessment findings into programmatic actions such as hiring applied-math faculty, integrating technology and group projects, improving career advising, and adjusting course placement and sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to consistent recommendations (e.g., technology integration, career information) with targeted interventions and monitor outcomes in subsequent assessment cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive examination design (written and oral)
rubrics_metrics.description: For comprehensive (comps), include a written major-specific component (two days, essays and problems) to review and test competence in the major and an oral 50-minute liberal-arts component examined by three faculty (major, minor, at-large) to probe reflective, integrative thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments decide written-format specifics each year (number of essays, topic selection, balance of calculus vs advanced topics); use comps results to inform curricular changes.
